questions.question: Which of the following Indian states recently became the second in the country, after Kerala, to publish a comprehensive State Bird Atlas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **In February 2026, Goa became the second state in India to release its own comprehensive Bird Atlas, following in the footsteps of Kerala.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The "Bird Atlas of Goa" was officially unveiled during the 9th Bird Festival of Goa, held on February 7, 2026, at Valpoi.**
 
• The atlas is a result of a massive **citizen science project** where volunteers and birdwatchers conducted grid-based scientific surveys across the state to map bird distribution and abundance.
 
• The theme of the 9th Bird Festival was **“Majestic Mhadei,”** focusing on the biodiversity of the Mhadei river basin.
 
• Significance of the Atlas__
 __
 
• It provides baseline data for long-term ecological monitoring and tracking changes in bird populations due to climate change or habitat loss.
 
• A companion book, **“Birds of Goa: Konkani Nomenclature – Olakh Suknayanchi,”** was also released to document bird names in the local Konkani language.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• First State with Bird Atlas__

 __
 
• **Kerala** was the first state in India to publish a state-level bird atlas (released in 2022), mapping the entire state’s avian diversity.
 
 
 
• Conservation Efforts__
 __
 
• During the festival, an MoU was signed between the **Goa Forest Department** and the **ResQ Charitable Trust** to strengthen wildlife rescue and rehabilitation in the state.
 
 
 
• Inauguration__
 
 
• The event was inaugurated by Goa's Chief Secretary, **C. Candavelou**, highlighting the government’s commitment to scientific wildlife documentation.

questions.question: Which city created a new Guinness World Record on 1 March 2026 by planting 2,51,446 saplings in just one hour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Varanasi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **World Record:** Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh achieved a historic **Guinness World Record** by planting **2,51,446 saplings** in a single hour, surpassing a record previously held by China for eight years.
 
• **Location:** The plantation drive took place in **Domari village** on the banks of the Ganga, covering 350 bighas of land.
 
• **Verification:** The feat was officially verified by Guinness World Records judge **Rishi Nath**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Highlights__**

__
 
• **Miyawaki Method:** The forest was created using the **Miyawaki technique**, which involves high-density, multi-species plantation for rapid forest growth.
 
• **Mini-Kashi Forest:** The site was divided into 60 sectors, each named after famous **Kashi Ghats** (e.g., Dashashwamedh, Manikarnika), creating a symbolic ecological landmark.
 
• **Diversity:** 27 native species were planted, including medicinal plants like **Ashwagandha** and timber trees like **Teak and Sheesham**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Significance__**

 
• **Participation:** Approximately **20,000 people** participated in this synchronized green initiative.
 
• **Ecological Restoration:** This project transforms a large tract of land into a planned **Urban Forest** to improve the local air quality and biodiversity along the river Ganga.

questions.question: Which Indian union territory assembly first adopted the National e‑Vidhan Application (NeVA) on 9 June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA):** NeVA is a **revolutionary initiative by the Government of India** aimed at digitizing the legislative assemblies across the country.
 
• Puducherry became the **first Union Territory** in India to adopt NeVA on **9 June 2025**, marking a significant step towards paperless governance.
 
• NeVA facilitates the **digitization of legislative assembly proceedings**, including discussions, bills, and other related documents, ensuring transparency and accessibility.
 
• The adoption of NeVA aligns with the government's vision of **Digital India**, promoting e-governance and reducing environmental impact.
 
• Under NeVA, legislators can access assembly proceedings and documents **electronically through tablets or laptops**, enhancing efficiency and reducing the dependency on physical documentation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of NeVA:**

 
 
• NeVA includes features such as **e-Voting, digital access to assembly agendas, and real-time updates** of legislative activities.
 
• The platform provides **multilingual support**, ensuring inclusivity for legislators from different linguistic backgrounds.
 
• It incorporates robust **security measures** to safeguard sensitive information and prevent unauthorized access.
 
• NeVA supports **archiving and retrieval** of legislative documents, allowing seamless access to historical records.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Digital Governance:**
 
 
• Digital governance systems like NeVA play a vital role in enhancing **accountability, transparency, and efficiency** in administrative processes.
 
• These initiatives contribute to **environmental sustainability** by reducing paper usage and promoting eco-friendly practices.
 
• They empower legislators and citizens by providing **easy access to information**, fostering participatory governance.
 
 
 
• **Puducherry:**
 
 
• Puducherry is a Union Territory located in southern India, comprising four regions: **Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam**.
 
• Known for its **French colonial heritage**, Puducherry has a unique cultural blend of Indian and French influences.
 
• The Union Territory has been proactive in adopting **technological advancements** to improve governance and public services.
 
 
 
• **Other Union Territories and States:**
 
 
• **Delhi:** Known as the National Capital Territory, Delhi is the political and administrative hub of India.
 
• **Lakshadweep:** An archipelago of islands in the Arabian Sea, Lakshadweep focuses on sustainable development due to its ecological sensitivity.
 
• **Chandigarh:** A union territory and the capital of Punjab and Haryana, Chandigarh is recognized for its modern urban planning and architecture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Digital India Initiative:**

 
 
• Launched in **2015**, the Digital India program aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• It focuses on **digital infrastructure, digital literacy, and digital delivery of services**.
 
• Adoption of platforms like NeVA is a step forward in achieving the objectives of Digital India.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The shift to paperless governance significantly reduces paper consumption, contributing to the conservation of natural resources.
 
• It aligns with global efforts to combat **climate change** and promote sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Efficiency:**
 
 
• Digitization of legislative processes enhances efficiency by enabling **quick access to documents and streamlined workflows**.
 
• It fosters better collaboration among legislators and supports informed decision-making.

questions.question: The Phase I of Noida International Airport (NIA), inaugurated in March 2026, has been developed under which of the following models?

• MRO Hub__

questions.question: Which city has launched India's first AI-powered door-to-door 'Saksham Skill Survey' to map the employability of youth at a ward level?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **First-of-its-kind Initiative:** **Mumbai** has become the first city in India to launch a localized, AI-driven door-to-door survey called the **'Saksham Skill Survey'**.
 
• **Pilot Ward:** The drive was inaugurated in the **H-West Ward**, which encompasses the Bandra, Khar, and Santacruz areas.
 
• **Target Demographic:** The survey specifically focuses on youth aged between **18 and 40 years** to assess their education, current skills, and employability potential.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Features & Goals__**

__
 
• **Workforce Intelligence:** The project uses **Artificial Intelligence** (powered by Sapio Analytics) to build a decentralized "Workforce Intelligence" model at the ward level.
 
• **Scope:** The survey aims to cover **55,000 households** through door-to-door enumeration to identify training needs.
 
• **Ambitious Targets:** The initiative seeks to provide specialized training to **15,000 candidates** and ensure **self-reliance or employment for 5,000** of them by 2027.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Significance of the Model__**

 
• **Decentralized Planning:** Unlike state-wide data, this ward-level mapping allows for highly **localized workforce planning** and micro-entrepreneurship opportunities.
 
• **Digital Transformation:** By integrating AI, the city can match local talent with specific industry requirements in real-time, reducing the "skill gap" often found in urban centers.
 
• **Scalability:** The H-West Ward project is a pilot intended to create a **replicable model** that can be scaled across other districts in Maharashtra and India.

questions.question: Where is the first police museum of Madhya Pradesh being built?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Betul**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **First Police Museum of Madhya Pradesh:** The first police museum in Madhya Pradesh is being constructed in **Betul district**. This significant initiative reflects the state's commitment to preserving and showcasing its policing history and achievements. 
• **Objective:** The museum is aimed at **highlighting the history, evolution, and contributions** of the police force in Madhya Pradesh, including artifacts, documents, and other memorabilia related to law enforcement. 
• **Location Selection:** Betul was chosen as the location due to its **historical importance** and strategic geographical placement, making it an ideal site for such a cultural and historical institution. 
• **Tourism and Education:** The museum will serve as a **tourist attraction** and an educational hub for visitors, researchers, and students interested in learning about the state’s police history. 
• **Infrastructure:** The museum is expected to feature **modern facilities** and interactive exhibits, ensuring an engaging experience for visitors while preserving historical artifacts. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Police Museums in India:** 
• **Delhi:** India’s first National Police Museum was established in New Delhi to showcase the history and evolution of policing in the country. 
• **Kolkata:** The Kolkata Police Museum displays rare artifacts and documents relating to the history of policing in the city. 
• Such museums aim to **educate the public** about the contributions of the police force and foster greater understanding and respect for law enforcement agencies. 
• **Significance of Police Museums:** 
• They preserve and showcase the **legacy of law enforcement**, including achievements, challenges, and innovations. 
• Provide insights into the **history and evolution** of policing methodologies and technologies. 
• Serve as a source of **inspiration and education** for law enforcement personnel and the general public. 
• **Betul District:** 
• Betul is located in the southern part of Madhya Pradesh and is known for its **historical significance** and cultural heritage. 
• The district is rich in **natural beauty** and attracts tourists for its forests, rivers, and ancient structures. 
• Establishing the police museum here is expected to boost **tourism and cultural awareness** in the region. 
• **Importance of Preserving Police History:** 
• Maintaining a police museum allows for the **documentation of the evolution** of law enforcement practices and technologies. 
• It provides a platform to **honor the sacrifices** and contributions of police officers over the years. 
• Educates the public about the **role of police** in maintaining law and order and fostering a sense of security. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Madhya Pradesh Tourism:** The state is known for its **rich cultural heritage**, historical monuments, and natural beauty, including sites like Khajuraho, Sanchi, and Bandhavgarh National Park. 
• **Police Reforms:** Madhya Pradesh has undertaken several initiatives to modernize its police force and improve law enforcement capabilities, including the use of **advanced technology** and training programs. 
• **Promotion of Museums:** Establishing museums dedicated to specific themes helps in promoting **education, tourism, and cultural awareness**. 
• **Contribution to Society:** Police museums play a crucial role in building a **positive image** of law enforcement agencies and fostering public trust.

questions.question: Which beach sand mineral found along Andhra Pradesh’s coastline is the primary source of rare earth elements (REEs) and thorium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monazite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Andhra Pradesh’s 974-km coastline** has gained strategic importance due to **large reserves of rare earth elements (REEs)** embedded in beach sand minerals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Monazite** is the **primary source of REEs and thorium** found in beach sand minerals.
 
• A **continuous mineral-rich belt** stretches from **Srikakulam to Nellore** along the coast.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh holds 30–35%** of India’s total **monazite reserves**.
 
• India’s total monazite reserves are estimated at **12–15 million tonnes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Other beach sand minerals include **ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, and sillimanite**.
 
• **REEs** are critical for **electronics, renewable energy, defence, and EV technologies**.
 
• Despite large reserves, the region remains a **largely underutilised critical mineral zone**.

questions.question: Which of the following districts was carved out most recently in Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arwal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arwal** district in Bihar was carved out of the Jehanabad district and established as a separate district in **2001**.
 
• It is located in central Bihar and is a relatively small district in terms of both area and population.
 
• The district headquarters of Arwal is in the town of Arwal, and it primarily consists of rural areas.
 
• This district was created to ensure better administrative efficiency and governance for the local population.
 
• Other options, such as Supaul, Sheohar, and Sheikhpura, were formed earlier than Arwal, making Arwal the most recently created among the options.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Supaul:**

 
 
• Supaul district was carved out of Saharsa district in **1991**.
 
• It is located in the northeastern part of Bihar and is part of the Kosi region.
 
• The Kosi river, known for its frequent flooding, flows through this district.
 
 
 
• **Sheohar:**
 
 
• Sheohar district was established in **1994** after being separated from Sitamarhi district.
 
• It is one of the smallest districts in Bihar and is located in the northern part of the state.
 
• The district is known for its agricultural activities, particularly the cultivation of maize and sugarcane.
 
 
 
• **Sheikhpura:**
 
 
• Sheikhpura district was formed in **2001**, the same year as Arwal, but prior to it.
 
• It was carved out of the Nalanda district in central Bihar.
 
• The district is known for its historical significance and cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Reorganization in Bihar:**
 
 
• Bihar has undergone several administrative reorganizations over the years to improve governance and development in smaller regions.
 
• Districts are often carved out based on factors such as population density, geographical area, and socio-economic needs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Formation of New Districts:**

 
 
• The formation of new districts is a common administrative practice in India to decentralize governance and improve service delivery.
 
• This process often involves the bifurcation of larger districts into smaller units for better administration.
 
 
 
• **Recent District Formations in Bihar:**
 
 
• The state government has focused on creating new districts to meet the growing administrative demands of the population.
 
• Efforts are made to ensure that newly created districts have adequate resources for governance and infrastructure development.

questions.question: Which state emerged as India’s first fully literate state, following a major literacy drive under the ULLAS scheme, in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, **Mizoram** was officially declared India's **first fully literate state** under the framework of the **ULLAS (Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society)** scheme.
 
• The declaration was made after the state achieved a literacy rate of more than **95%**, the benchmark prescribed for attaining full literacy.
 
• The achievement was the result of extensive efforts by the **School Education Department**, local communities, volunteers, and literacy workers across the state.
 
• The **ULLAS scheme**, launched by the **Ministry of Education**, focuses on adult education and lifelong learning opportunities for citizens aged **15 years and above**.
 
• Mizoram's strong educational culture, community participation, and effective implementation of literacy programs played a crucial role in achieving this milestone.
 
• ***Hence, Mizoram became India's first fully literate state in May 2025.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ULLAS Scheme:**

 
 
• ULLAS stands for **Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society**.
 
• Launched in **2022** for the period **2022–2027**.
 
• Implemented by the **Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education**.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of ULLAS:**
 
 
• Foundational literacy and numeracy.
 
• Critical life skills.
 
• Basic education.
 
• Vocational skills development.
 
• Continuing education and lifelong learning.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram:**
 
 
• Capital: **Aizawl**.
 
• Statehood attained on **20 February 1987**.
 
• Known for having one of the highest literacy rates in India.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Benchmark:**
 
 
• Under the ULLAS framework, a literacy rate of **95% or above** is considered the threshold for full literacy.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Improves employability, social awareness, and economic development.
 
• Promotes inclusive growth and citizen empowerment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **State Declared Fully Literate:** **Mizoram**.
 
• **Declaration Month:** **May 2025**.
 
• **Scheme Involved:** **ULLAS**.
 
• **Literacy Threshold:** **95%**.
 
• **Implementing Ministry:** **Ministry of Education, Government of India**.

questions.question: Which state approved the Freedom of Religion Bill 2026 to curb forced religious conversions and address "Changai Sabha" activities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Chhattisgarh Cabinet, led by CM Vishnu Deo Sai, approved the draft of the Chhattisgarh Freedom of Religion Bill 2026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Objective:** To prohibit religious conversions facilitated through **force, allurement, fraud, or misrepresentation**.
 
• **Targeted Provisions:** The bill includes specific measures to deal with **"Changai Sabhas"** (healing congregations) used for misleading people.
 
• **Legal Evolution:** This new bill aims to replace and strengthen the older **Chhattisgarh Freedom of Religion Act of 1968**.
 
• **Administrative Reforms:** Along with this bill, the cabinet approved the formation of the **Chhattisgarh Staff Selection Board** for Grade-III and IV recruitments.
 
• **Integrity in Exams:** The cabinet also cleared the **Anti-Paper Leak Law** (Prevention of Unfair Means in Public Recruitment Bill 2026).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Anti-Conversion Laws in India__

 __
 
• Several Indian states, including UP, MP, and Karnataka, have passed similar "Freedom of Religion" laws to regulate conversions, often citing the protection of tribal cultures and preventing communal tension.
 
 
 
• Bastar Region__
 
 
• A tribal-dominated area in Chhattisgarh where issues of religious conversion and cultural identity have been subjects of significant socio-political debate.

questions.question: Where is the 3.5-kilometre emergency landing facility located on the newly inaugurated Ganga Expressway?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shahjahanpur district**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** inaugurated the ambitious **Ganga Expressway** and launched multiple development projects in **Uttar Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Emergency Landing Facility:** A major strategic feature of the **Ganga Expressway** is a specially designed **3.5-kilometre emergency landing facility**.
 
• This landing facility is located in the **Shahjahanpur district**.

questions.question: Which of the following two states have jointly conducted a Nilgiri Tahr census in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala and Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nilgiri Tahr Census:** The **Nilgiri Tahr census** is a joint initiative conducted by the states of **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu** in **April 2025**. The primary objective is to estimate the population and study the distribution of the **Nilgiri Tahr**, an endangered species endemic to the **Western Ghats**.
 
• **Collaboration:** Both states collaborated in **April 2025** to undertake a comprehensive survey of the species. This effort highlights their commitment to preserving biodiversity in the ecologically sensitive **Western Ghats**.
 
• **Ecological Importance:** The **Nilgiri Tahr** is classified as **Endangered** under the **IUCN Red List** due to habitat loss and declining population. The census is essential for evaluating existing conservation measures and developing future strategies.
 
• **Habitat:** The species is predominantly found in the **Nilgiri Hills** and other parts of the **Western Ghats**, which span across **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu**. These regions are known for their rich biodiversity and unique ecosystems.
 
• **Protected Areas:** Conservation efforts include protected areas like **Eravikulam National Park** in Kerala and **Mukurthi National Park** in Tamil Nadu, which are critical habitats for the **Nilgiri Tahr**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nilgiri Tahr:**

 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr** is a mountain goat-like ungulate species endemic to the **Western Ghats** of India.
 
• **Scientific Name:** *Nilgiritragus hylocrius*.
 
• It is the **state animal** of Tamil Nadu and primarily inhabits high-altitude **grasslands** and rocky areas.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Status:**
 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr** is classified as **Endangered** under the **IUCN Red List**, with major threats including habitat destruction, poaching, and livestock competition.
 
 
 
• **Key Protected Areas:**
 
 
• **Eravikulam National Park:** Located in Kerala, this park hosts the **largest population** of Nilgiri Tahr.
 
• **Mukurthi National Park:** Situated in Tamil Nadu, it is another critical habitat for the species.
 
• **Silent Valley National Park:** Located in Kerala, contributing significantly to biodiversity conservation.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr Recovery Program** was launched to monitor and protect the species.
 
• Regular **censuses** and **habitat restoration initiatives** are being carried out by both state governments.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• The **Western Ghats** is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known for its exceptional biodiversity and is one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity globally.
 
• It spans across six Indian states: **Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, and Gujarat**.
 
• It is the origin of many perennial rivers such as **Godavari, Kaveri, and Krishna**, essential for agriculture and drinking water.
 
• Threats include **deforestation**, **climate change**, and **human encroachment**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Importance of Biodiversity Conservation:**

 
 
• The **Nilgiri Tahr census** is a vital step towards understanding and conserving endangered species in the **Western Ghats**.
 
• Efforts like afforestation, strict wildlife protection laws, and the establishment of protected areas are essential to mitigate biodiversity loss.
 
 
 
• **Role of State Collaboration:**
 
 
• The collaboration between **Kerala** and **Tamil Nadu** showcases the importance of joint efforts in addressing ecological challenges.
